answer.rationale: Finance requires an 18% spend cut in 14 days and the low-cost vendor's standalone quote already meets it. memory_c2 supports a primary switch to a low-cost vendor with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing. However, the line is running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, so I cannot absorb the migration risk of a full primary switch. memory_c3 supports adding a second source to de-risk constrained components, which is the pattern I want to apply here as a parallel hedge. Plan: lead with switch_primary_vendor on a small guarded test lot first to validate the cost saving in production, and in parallel begin qualifying the low-cost vendor as a second source to remove single-point-of-failure exposure. Delivery risk to the 94% volume is preserved because incumbent supply continues for the bulk of volume during the test. If the test passes, broaden the switch in the next cycle; if it fails, I have memory_c4 and memory_c6 available to renegotiate or extend with the incumbent. I am not committing to a full switch yet, and I am not renewing the incumbent outright because that would miss the finance mandate. I am not deferring because the contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew. memory_c5 deferral logic does not apply when a hard expiry is in play.
